title: Smart Watermark Coordinator for continuous batching and KV compaction
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response length workloads drive unstable batch formation and uneven KV residency on GPUs. Short-turn requests get coalesced into large batches with long turns, increasing latency and forcing aggressive KV eviction. Long-turn-heavy batches cause GPU memory pressure and occasional OOMs during peak bursts.

Goal: Implement a Smart Watermark Coordinator (SWC) inside the continuous batching scheduler to coordinate per-slot watermarks, trigger KV compaction proactively, and dynamically rebalance GPU slab reservations to reduce tail latency and KV eviction without sacrificing throughput.

Success metrics (canary baseline -> target):
- p95 latency for short-turn flows: 220ms -> 160ms (<= -27%)
- p99 latency overall: 1.85s -> <= 1.4s
- KV eviction rate per-GPU during peak 5-min windows: 18% -> <= 7%
- Token throughput (tokens/sec/GPU): within +/-5% of baseline
- OOM incidents: 1/month -> 0 in rollout window

Scope: scheduler + kv manager changes only. No model code changes. Must be compatible with Hosted and Dedicated modes. Work includes design, simulator experiments on archived traces, runtime implementation, perf tests on staging cluster, gradual canary rollout, monitoring and rollback criteria.

Design summary:
1) Per-slot watermarks: compute two watermarks per GPU slot: short-watermark (optimizes latency for short prompts) and long-watermark (optimizes utilization for long responses). The coordinator maintains ephemeral weights per slot derived from recent turn-length histogram and request priority.
2) Watermark gating: when a short-priority request arrives, it can preempt the long-watermark window if coordinator estimates net latency benefit. Preemption is soft: allow early flush with a configurable penalty budget to avoid throughput collapse.
3) Proactive KV compaction: SWC signals KV manager to run lightweight compaction when projected residency exceeds a threshold for N consecutive windows. Compaction is staged: trimming low-reuse entries first, then compacting KV slabs to free contiguous GPU memory for long-turn allocations.
4) Slab rebalance: coordinate with the GPU memory allocator to temporarily borrow slab quotas between slots where adaptive demand patterns are detected. Borrowing has a TTL and can be revoked on SLO violations.
5) Feedback loop and safety gates: closed-loop regulator uses moving-window metrics (batch size distribution, KV hit rate, per-slot latency) to adjust watermark heuristics. Safety gates enforce maximum eviction and minimum throughput tolerances.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive early flush reduces short-tail latency but increases scheduling overhead and could reduce sequential-token locality for long turns.
- Proactive compaction reduces fragmentation and OOM risk but incurs additional compute/latency overhead during compaction cycles. We bias compaction to low-traffic windows and use soft compaction ops when possible.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 0 (design & simulator): 2w: build trace-driven simulator (based on archived production traces) to evaluate watermark policies and compaction thresholds.
- Phase 1 (impl): 2w: implement SWC control plane and scheduler hooks in runtime, add KV compaction API. Unit tests and feature flags.
- Phase 2 (staging perf): 1w: run synthetic and traced canary workloads on staging cluster (3 GPUs), iterate thresholds.
- Phase 3 (canary rollout): 1w: 5% traffic in hosted region + 2 Dedicated pods with canary config. Monitor metrics and abort on trigger conditions.
- Phase 4 (ramp): 2w: expand to 25%/50% then 100% if stable.

Monitoring and rollback:
- Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 per-route, per-slot GPU memory usage, KV eviction rate, batch size histogram, token throughput.
- Alert triggers (auto-rollback if any fires during canary):
  - p95 increase > 15% vs baseline for >= 5m
  - KV eviction rate > +10pp vs baseline for >= 3m
  - Any OOM or model crash
  - Token throughput drop > 10% sustained 10m

Backward compatibility: SWC behind feature flag and can be disabled per-cluster. Default disabled for on-prem customers until validated.

Open questions:
- Threshold selection: what moving-window (30s, 60s, 5m) offers best stability? Initial sim uses 60s.
- Priority mapping: how to surface priority for multi-tenant workloads (tenant importance vs flow length)?
- Telemetry overhead: compaction signals and per-slot histograms increase telemetry volume; need sampling strategy.

Deliverables:
- Confluence design doc with diagrams
- Simulator code and results (archived traces + scripts)
- Runtime implementation + tests
- Staging perf report + canary playbook
